title: Frontend Frameworks
description: Component UIs in React: props, state, hooks, effects, lists, rendering performance, and SSR.

questions.prompt: In this React component, the item is deleted as soon as the list renders, and clicking the button does nothing. Which change fixes it?

options.text: Use the lowercase DOM name: onclick={onDelete()}
Pass the function instead of calling it: onClick={onDelete}
Add type="button" so the click does not submit a form
Move the onDelete() call into a useEffect after render

questions.explanation: onDelete() runs during render and passes its return value (undefined) as the handler. React needs a function reference, either onDelete or () => onDelete(). type="button" matters inside forms but does not stop the call during render.

questions.prompt: In React, the parent owns count and passes it down. Clicking this button never changes the displayed number. What is the idiomatic fix?

options.text: Have the parent pass an onIncrement callback that updates its state, and call it on click
Write count += 1 instead, because React tracks assignments to props but not ++
Copy count into a module-level variable and increment that variable on click
Call this.forceUpdate() after count++ so React re-renders with the new value

questions.explanation: Props are read-only snapshots; changing the local variable neither updates the parent's state nor triggers a render. Data flows down and events flow up: the state owner exposes a callback. forceUpdate exists only on class components and would still render the parent's unchanged value.

questions.prompt: This React component crashes with "Rendered more hooks than during the previous render" right after the user logs in. What is the cause?

options.text: useState cannot take a string initial value; it must be initialized with null or an object
The early return must render null rather than JSX whenever a component uses any hooks
useState runs only on some renders; hooks must be called unconditionally before any early return
setTab is passed to a child component, but hook setters may only be called in their own component

questions.explanation: React identifies hooks by call order, so the number and order of hook calls must be identical on every render (Rules of Hooks). Move useState above the if. Passing a setter to a child is normal and safe.

questions.prompt: Typing into this React search box does nothing: the field stays empty. Which change fixes it while keeping query as the source of truth?

options.text: Replace value={query} with defaultValue={query} on the input
Initialize the state with useState(null) instead of an empty string
Add readOnly={false} so React allows the input to be edited
Add onChange={(e) => setQuery(e.target.value)} to the input

questions.explanation: A value prop makes the input controlled: React re-applies query on every render, and nothing ever updates query. An onChange that sets state completes the loop. defaultValue makes it uncontrolled, so typing works but query never changes.

questions.prompt: True or false: in this React component, addItem reliably re-renders the list with the new item.
questions.explanation: push mutates the existing array, and setItems receives the same reference, so React's Object.is comparison sees no change and can skip the render. Create a new array instead: setItems([...items, item]) or setItems((prev) => [...prev, item]).

questions.prompt: This React component should fetch the user once per userId. The network tab shows requests firing endlessly. Which line is wrong?
questions.explanation: With no dependency array the effect runs after every render, and setUser causes another render (a new object each time), so it loops forever. It should close with }, [userId]); so it re-runs only when userId changes.

questions.prompt: In development with StrictMode this React clock ticks twice per second, and in production the interval keeps running after the component unmounts. What is the correct fix?

options.text: Keep the interval id and return () => clearInterval(id) from the effect
Remove StrictMode, since it is the cause of the extra interval
Add now to the dependency array so the interval stays in sync
Switch to useLayoutEffect so the interval is created only once

questions.explanation: Every effect that subscribes to something needs a cleanup. StrictMode deliberately mounts, unmounts, and remounts in development to expose missing cleanups like this one; removing it hides the bug but production unmounts still leak.

questions.prompt: After the user deletes the first todo, the input in the first row still shows the deleted todo's text and the last todo's text disappears. What is the cause?

options.text: defaultValue only works inside a <form>; wrap the list in a form element
remove(todo.id) captures a stale id; pass index to remove instead
key={index} makes React match rows by position and reuse their inputs; use key={todo.id}
React cannot remove list items; filter todos with CSS display: none

questions.explanation: Keys tell React which item each element belongs to. With index keys, deleting item 0 looks like "the last row was removed," so rows 0 and 1 keep their existing uncontrolled inputs. Stable ids keep each input attached to its own todo.

questions.prompt: A reviewer flags this React component. What change do the React docs recommend?

options.text: Move the calculation into useLayoutEffect so the stale total is not painted before it updates
Compute total during render (with useMemo only if it is expensive) and delete the state and effect
Add total to the dependency array so that the effect re-runs whenever the total changes
Copy items into state as well so that items and total always update in the same render

questions.explanation: Values derivable from props or state should be calculated while rendering ("You Might Not Need an Effect"). Syncing them through state and an effect causes an extra render with a stale total and invites drift. useLayoutEffect still does the redundant render.

questions.prompt: In React, which of these cause a function component to re-render? Select all that apply.

options.text: Calling its own state setter with a different value
Mutating ref.current on a ref created with useRef
Its parent re-renders (the component is not wrapped in memo)
A context it reads with useContext receives a new value
A module-level variable that it reads is reassigned

questions.explanation: React re-renders on state changes, parent renders (by default children render too), and changes to consumed context. Refs and plain variables are invisible to React: changing them does not schedule a render.

questions.prompt: When a user has no notifications, a stray "0" appears next to the bell icon. Which change fixes it?

options.text: Use {count || <Badge value={count} />}
Use {count ?? <Badge value={count} />}
Use {!count && <Badge value={count} />}
Use {count > 0 && <Badge value={count} />}

questions.explanation: count && ... evaluates to 0 when count is 0, and React renders the number 0 (it only skips false, null, undefined, and true). A boolean condition such as count > 0 renders nothing. The other options render the 0 or show the badge at the wrong time.

questions.prompt: The React Profiler shows every Row re-rendering whenever selected changes, even though Row is wrapped in memo. Why?

options.text: onSelect and style are new objects on every render, so memo's shallow prop comparison fails
memo only skips renders for class components; function components always re-render
memo compares props deeply, and the items array is recreated whenever selected changes
Using item.id as the key forces a fresh render; memo only works with index-based keys

questions.explanation: memo compares each prop with Object.is; an inline arrow and an inline object literal are new references every render. Hoist the style constant and pass a stable callback (useCallback taking the id as an argument). memo is shallow, not deep, and items is unchanged here.

questions.prompt: This React counter shows 1 and then stops increasing. Which change fixes it while keeping a single interval for the component's lifetime?

options.text: Add count to the dependency array of the effect
Store the interval id in useRef instead of a const
Use the updater form: setCount((c) => c + 1)
Move setInterval out of the effect into the body

questions.explanation: The interval callback closed over count from the first render (0), so it keeps setting 1. The updater form reads the latest state without depending on count. Adding count to the dependencies also works but tears down and recreates the interval every tick, which the prompt rules out.

questions.prompt: When a user types quickly, this React component sometimes shows results for an older query. What is the recommended fix?

options.text: Remove query from the dependency array so that only one request is ever in flight at a time
Wrap setResults in startTransition so React applies the result updates in request order
Switch to useLayoutEffect so each fetch finishes before the next render is allowed to start
Return a cleanup that sets an ignore flag (or aborts the request) and skip setResults for stale responses

questions.explanation: Responses can resolve out of order. When query changes, React runs the previous effect's cleanup, so flagging or aborting there guarantees only the latest response is applied (React docs, "Fetching data" with an ignore flag). startTransition affects render priority, not network ordering.

questions.prompt: A server-rendered React page (e.g., Next.js) shows hydration-mismatch errors for this component. Which approach correctly resolves it?

options.text: Add suppressHydrationWarning to the root <html> element so all child mismatches are ignored
Render a placeholder first, then set the time in state from a useEffect after mount
Wrap the value in useMemo(() => new Date(), []) so it is computed only once per page load
Wrap the component in StrictMode so React reconciles server and client output automatically

questions.explanation:
The server and the browser compute different times (and possibly locales), so the first client render does not match the server HTML. Effects run only on the client after hydration, so setting the time there keeps the initial render identical. suppressHydrationWarning only applies one level deep, so on it does not cover this

.
